chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abdullah ibn Waddah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who died leaving behind her husband, her mother, and her father, he said: 'She is from six shares: for the husband is half, three shares; and for the mother is one-third, two shares; and for the father is one-sixth, one share.'
ai.seo_question: How is a woman's estate distributed when she leaves behind a husband, mother, and father?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific shares of the husband, mother, and father when all three coexist, establishing the father's share as a fixed one-sixth (suds) rather than a residual heir in this configuration. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the father's status from the mother's, who receives one-third of the estate, while the husband takes the remaining half. The hadith serves as a practical application of the general inheritance rules found in Surah An-Nisa, providing precise fractional allocations for complex family structures.
